entities.summary: Pope Alexander VI was the head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States from 11 August 1492 until his death in 1503. He was born unknown and died on 28 August 1503. Alexander VI was a key figure in the Renaissance and played a significant role in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire. He was the son of Rodrigo Borgia and Vannozza dei Cattanei, and his election as Pope was marked by controversy and power struggles. As Pope, Alexander VI supported the Spanish Inquisition and clashed with the Holy Roman Emperor, Maximilian I. He also launched a series of military campaigns against the Ottoman Empire. The Pope's policies and actions had a lasting impact on the Catholic Church and the political landscape of Europe. He was succeeded by Pope Pius III, who was elected after Alexander VI's death. The Pope's legacy is still debated among historians today.
